newsitem.title: USA: GM Ft. Wayne plant hit by UAW strike.
newsitem.headline: GM Ft. Wayne plant hit by UAW strike.

text.p: United Auto Workers members walked off the job at a General Motors Corp pickup truck plant in Ft. Wayne, Ind., after a 1000 EST/1500 GMT strike deadline expired, a spokeswoman for the union said Friday.
"All I know is they're on strike," said a woman who answered the phone at UAW Local 2209, where about 2,700 members work at the plant.

Negotiators talked through the night but were unable to reach an agreement on a new three-year contract, said a union spokesman. The plant makes about 1,000 regular cab Chevrolet C/K and GMC Sierra full-size pickup trucks a day.

The UAW wants GM to hire more workers at the plant to cut down on the overtime it has been running and address health and safety issues. It is the first strike over local contract terms since GM and the UAW reached a national agreement on a new three-year pact last November.
GM has local agreements with about 60 percent of its 105 UAW locals around the country. Talks at the locals have been proceeding slowly, the union has said.
The Ft. Wayne facility is the only one of GM's light truck plants that makes just regular cab full-size pickup trucks, which tend to be less popular than extended cab models.
GM makes extended cab and short box versions at its plant in Oshawa, Ontario. It produces both regular and extended cab models in Pontiac, Mich., and heavy-duty pickup trucks in Flint, Mich.

At the beginning of February, C/K and Sierra pickup trucks overall had a more than 90-day supply on dealer lots, although that is believed to have come down since then. The industry considers a 60-day supply to be ideal.
